headline: session-continue.sh blocks a stop in 4 ways, each emitting decision:"block" while the process exits 0. (1) The agent-armed continuation sentinel, emitted at 1331-1336 and disabled by a kill phrase, `clear`, CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX or the SID-bind check. (2) The mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's own uncommitted writes, which arms at 1072 and uses the same emit, disabled by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or CC_MECH_MAX. (3) The ship floor for 📦/🚀 own work at 1199, disabled by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX. (4) The wake floor for going idle with no inbox watcher at 894-895, disabled by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX or CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop in 5 cases, emitted from 3 places (lines 1334/1336, 1199, 895). The cases are: an armed continuation sentinel (1334/1336, capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX); an auto-armed sentinel for uncommitted files this session edited (off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0); the ship floor for committed-but-unlanded work (1199); the ship floor for landed-but-not-live work (1199), both off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR≠1; and the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (895, off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR≠1). A kill phrase in the operator's last message overrides all five, and the exit-2 paths only run from the command line, never on a Stop.

The Stop hook can block a stop under 5 conditions, and every block is printed JSON {decision:"block"} followed by exit 0 (never exit 2): (1) the agent has armed a 🔧 sentinel (emitted at lines 1334/1336; disabled by a kill phrase, `clear`, a sid mismatch, or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap, where 0 turns it off); (2) the hook arms that sentinel itself when the session has its own uncommitted edits (line 1072, then 1334/1336; CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 turns it off, CC_MECH_MAX caps it); (3) the 📦 ship floor on unlanded commits and (4) the 🚀 ship floor on unconverged landed work (both line 1199, printed at 1212; CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 turns them off, CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX caps them, and they do not re-fire on the same HEAD sha); (5) the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (lines 894-895, printed at 1217; CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0 turns it off, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX caps it, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S backs it off). An operator kill phrase suppresses all 5.

They are: an agent-armed sentinel under the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap (:1334/1336); the mechanical 🔧 auto-arm when this session left its own writes uncommitted (armed :1072, CC_MECH_CONTINUE/CC_MECH_MAX); the ship floor on 📦 own unlanded commits and on 🚀 not-live (both :1199, CC_SHIP_FLOOR/CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX); and the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (:895, CC_WAKE_FLOOR/_MAX/_TTL_S). The operator kill-switch phrase overrides all of them.

I found five conditions under which session-continue.sh blocks a stop; each prints {decision:"block"} and the hook always exits 0 on the Stop path. (1) An agent-armed 🔧 sentinel, emitted at line 1336/1334: stopped by a kill phrase, a sid mismatch or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap (default 8). (2) The mechanical 🔧 arm for uncommitted files this session wrote, which blocks through that same path: off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, budget CC_MECH_MAX. (3) and (4) The ship floor for 📦 and 🚀, emitted at line 1199: off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0, budget CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX. (5) The wake floor, emitted at lines 894-895: off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, limited by CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX and CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S. The operator kill phrase (KILL_RE, line 348) suppresses all five. This comes from reading the code only; nothing was run.

All four floors stand down on an operator kill phrase.

I found 8 real bugs in rotate-logs.sh (by reading the code, not running it). The worst are on line 5, where a missing or failed cd goes unchecked and line 11 then deletes .gz files in the wrong directory, and on line 11, where tail -n +$keep keeps only keep-1 archives, xargs splits filenames on spaces, and the *.gz glob also catches unrelated archives. The rest are a gzip name clash that stops repeat rotation, -mtime +1 meaning 2 days, and unsafe word splitting on lines 6-7.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs. The worst is the unchecked, unquoted `cd $dir`: a missing or empty argument makes the script gzip logs and delete .gz files in the wrong directory (HOME or the caller's cwd). The rest are `xargs rm` splitting names on whitespace, an off-by-one in `tail` that keeps one archive too few, `-mtime +1` meaning 48 h rather than 1 day, `$(ls)` and the unquoted test breaking on odd filenames, gzip refusing to overwrite an existing archive so later rotations never happen, and a success message printed even when steps fail.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs, most severe first: (1) line 5's unchecked, unquoted `cd` means line 11 deletes .gz files in the wrong directory; (2) gzip hits an existing archive name, so a log is never rotated again; (3) `tail -n +$keep` keeps one archive too few; (4) the `*.gz` glob prunes unrelated archives; (5) `-mtime +1` waits 2 days, not 1; (6) `ls` and word-splitting break on spaces and leading dashes; (7) it reports success and exits 0 even when a step failed.

A static read of rotate-logs.sh found 6 real bugs (none run or measured): the worst is that an unchecked, unquoted `cd $dir` can gzip logs and delete archives in $HOME or the current directory; `tail -n +$keep` is off by one and keeps only keep-1 archives; xargs splits names on whitespace and can delete the wrong files; `-mtime +1` skips logs 24-48h old; the loop and test break on names with spaces or a leading dash; and gzip refuses to overwrite an existing .gz, so rotation never builds a history.
